articles.title: Following a terrorist attack and with three Islamists sentenced to death by hanging, Jordan cancels Christmas celebrations
articles.description: In an unusual display of consensus, Jordan’s Council of Church Leaders, joined by evangelical communities, opted to cancel public Christmas festivities throughout the country while maintaining the liturgical life of the churches. Christmas Masses, pastoral activities and charitable services will continue, but celebrations are being deliberately stripped of their usual public dimension. articles.title: 11 Injured in Houthi Terrorist Attack on Riyadh Financial District Tower
articles.description: The General Directorate of Civil Defense said 11 people were injured on Tuesday when a tower in Riyadh's financial district was targeted in a terrorist attack by the Houthi militia. The injured are two Saudi citizens and nine residents: two Indians, three Nepalis, and four Egyptians, according to SPA. The relevant authorities responded immediately, followed all approved procedures for such incidents, and took the necessary measures to protect lives and property.

articles.title: Saudi condemns ‘terrorist attack’ after Riyadh skyscraper hit twice in a week
articles.description: The tallest skyscraper in Saudi Arabia’s capital of Riyadh was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, witnesses said, as the coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”. Three separate witnesses said the strike targeted the 80-storey Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower, which houses the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund and dominates Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD).
